solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Byzantine cleric's dear treasure

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters of the next two words are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An Orthodox priest from Byzantium holds something dear and treasured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Byzantine' looks like it simply describes the cleric, but it is the anagram signal for CLERIC'S DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy relic is something a church guards and venerates, a prized object kept as a treasure.

clue.text: Dickens' Heep is humble; somewhat timid …

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Uriah Heep, the falsely 'umble clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield, comes across as rather timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shy and easily embarrassed is bashful and timid in manner.

clue.text: … shy, hiding awkward drawl, lacking courage

indicators.note: one word hides the other, which sits wholly inside it

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful

indicators.note: an awkward drawl is a clumsy one, so its letters are put clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 Down: a shy person mumbles in an awkward drawl, lacking the nerve to speak up.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 1 Down's timid Heep; 'awkward' is the anagram signal, not a description of the drawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is someone without bravery, so being without courage is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Boredom leads to English neo- Nazi urging insurrection

indicators.note: the leads of a group of words are their front letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: Bored young English extremists drift toward neo-Nazi calls for revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loan word for listless weariness and lack of interest, which is what boredom is.

clue.text: Confirmation of right to hold gun overturned

indicators.note: one piece is made to hold another within it
in a down clue, overturned turns the word for gun upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun, especially a handgun

explanation.surface: A document confirming the right to carry a firearm has been overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: RT (right) holds ECEIP, PIECE turned over by 'overturned'.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is written proof that payment was made or goods were delivered: a confirmation.

clue.text: German scientist left warning light on top of transponder

parts.note: an amber traffic light warns that the signal is about to change

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A German physicist mounts a warning lamp on a radio transponder.
explanation.walkthrough: Johann Heinrich Lambert was an 18th-century German mathematician and physicist; a unit of brightness is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambert, a German polymath of the 1700s, worked on light and proved pi irrational, so he is a German scientist.

clue.text: Burden Julius had reportedly to bear, being optically challenged

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden one must endure

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, so the spoken form stands in for another spelling

parts.note: the setter Julius speaking of himself would say I'd, short for I had

explanation.surface: The setter Julius moans about the burden he carries, a problem with his eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: I'D, what Julius would say for 'I had', said out loud gives EYED. 'to bear' only joins the pieces, echoing the phrase 'a cross to bear'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-eyed person has a squint, a defect of vision, which is a jokey way of being challenged in sight.

clue.text: Article about Henry Lawrence

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials TE
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance; that the answer also runs across 'about Henry' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a man called Henry Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the definite article is one of the two kinds of article in English.

clue.text: A bit squiffy with 10cl on board, neat

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, as cargo is carried within a ship

parts.note: neat and tidy both mean orderly
ten centilitres is one decilitre, abbreviated dl

explanation.surface: A drinker is slightly squiffy after downing 10cl of spirit, taken neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like describing an undiluted drink, but it supplies TIDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, which is what being a little squiffy means.

clue.text: A sailor about to turn up in bloomers

indicators.note: in a down clue, to turn up means the whole string reads upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A sailor is about to show up in women's baggy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear, but here it means blunders. A, TAR and RE read upwards give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are lists of mistakes in a printed book, and bloomers is British slang for blunders or mistakes.

clue.text: Chap's losing bet on 2015's General Election …

definitions.meaning: a male first name, standing for any fellow
Ed Miliband led Labour into the 2015 UK election and lost, so backing him to win was a losing wager

explanation.surface: A man laments the money he lost backing the wrong side in the 2015 British election.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ED WIN, the name reads as a bet that Ed Miliband, Labour leader, would win the 2015 UK general election; David Cameron won it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin is a man's given name, so it stands for a chap; split in two it is a punt on Ed winning.

clue.text: … filmed by the winner using this?

definitions.text: filmed by the winner using this?

parts.words: filmed by the winner using this?
parts.note: the clue continues from 9 Across: the winner of 2015 was David Cameron, whose name begins like the device a home film is shot on

explanation.surface: Continuing 9 Across: the election victor recorded the night on a home video camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The winner in 2015 was David Cameron, and his name starts with CAM, as does the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable video camera with its own recorder is what anyone, election winner or not, would film with.

clue.text: I gather Ms Hilton considered killing her father

indicators.note: I gather here means I hear it said, so the words are judged by their spoken sound

parts.note: Paris Hilton, the American socialite; considered means eyed, so the phrase is Paris eyed

explanation.surface: Gossip suggests the heiress Paris Hilton once contemplated killing her own father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gather' looks like hearsay about Paris Hilton but signals the spoken form: PARIS EYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Parricide is the murder of a parent or close relative, so the slaying of a father is one instance.

clue.text: Leave Diocletian's retirement home

definitions.meaning: to go away or depart, as in slang 'let's go'
the Roman emperor Diocletian retired to his palace on the Dalmatian coast, around which the Croatian city grew

explanation.surface: Someone is told to depart from the Roman emperor Diocletian's place of retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is both slang for depart and the Croatian port city built within Diocletian's palace.

clue.text: Shop to have nothing on the shelves

definitions.meaning: to shop someone is British slang for informing on or betraying them
a store that has sold its whole stock has nothing left to display

explanation.surface: A shop is about to run out of all its stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like a store, but as a verb it is British slang for betraying someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell out is both to betray, which shop means as slang, and to sell every item in stock.

clue.text: Grey-green wild boar gobbles Old Nick up

indicators.note: to gobble is to swallow, so one piece takes the other inside it
wild means out of control, so the letters of boar run riot into a new order
in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil

explanation.surface: A wild boar devours the Devil, all in a drab grey-green setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' is the anagram signal and 'up' reverses Old Nick, since this is a down clue; 'gobbles' puts the reversed piece inside after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is the dull greenish-grey colour of military uniforms, a shade of grey-green.

clue.text: Starts to throw out young son's playthings

indicators.note: the starts of the words that follow are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A child begins throwing out his young son's playthings.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys are objects children play with, a direct synonym of playthings.

clue.text: Christian name for Irish county's new church

parts.note: Clare is a county on the west coast of Ireland
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A newly built church in an Irish county is given a Christian name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarence is a male first name, and a first name is called a Christian name.

clue.text: A few more pages thrown in to madden Dumbledore

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into the text, sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Extra pages are added to a Harry Potter book just to irritate the wizard Dumbledore.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is a supplement of extra material added to a book, a few more pages.

clue.text: Beastly British rugby tourist trashed centre of European capital

indicators.note: the centre of the city's name is trashed, its middle letters thrown away

parts.note: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal

explanation.surface: A rowdy British rugby fan on tour wrecks the middle of a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish Lions are the touring rugby team; 'Beastly' is there because a lion is a beast. Removing the middle SB from LISBON leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Players picked for the British and Irish rugby tour are called Lions, and a lion is a beast.

clue.text: Surrounded by rebel cannon, Duke disobeys orders

definitions.note: the clue gives a verb phrase where the answer is the refusal itself, a phrase said when declining an order

indicators.note: one piece is surrounded on both sides by the other
to rebel is to rise against the existing order, so the letters break ranks into a new arrangement

parts.note: the setter's slip: these letters are meant to supply two Os and two Ns, but have one O and three Ns

explanation.surface: Faced with rebel artillery, a duke refuses his orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebel' is meant to rearrange 'cannon' round the D, but as printed it has three Ns and one O where two of each are needed: the setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal phrase of refusal, what someone says when declining to carry out an order.

clue.text: Plastered with rouge, the home secretary went first

parts.note: Amber Rudd was British Home Secretary when the puzzle appeared
to lead is to go first, past tense led

explanation.surface: The Home Secretary, heavily made up, went first.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruddle is red ochre used for marking sheep, so ruddled means reddened with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddled means smeared with ruddle, red ochre, so heavily coated in red as with rouge.

clue.text: Cliff right above entrance to idyllic Somerset town

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece above another comes before it
the entrance to a word is its first letter

parts.note: Chard is a market town in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: A cliff stands just right of the way into a lovely Somerset town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff' looks like a rock face but means the singer Sir Cliff Richard, a British pop star since the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliff Richard is a veteran British pop singer, so Cliff is a first name paired with this surname.

clue.text: Footballer least likely to be transferred?

definitions.text: Footballer least likely to be transferred?

parts.words: Footballer least likely to be transferred?
parts.note: the player in goal is a footballer, and the word also names a possession one holds on to rather than lets another club have

explanation.surface: Which footballer is the club least likely to sell?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about a transfer-market star, but the answer is the goal's guardian, whose title also describes something you retain rather than let go.
explanation.definitionFit: The player in goal is a footballer, and the word also means something worth retaining, never transferred.

clue.text: Condemned party's revolutionary protest

parts.note: a do is a party; the 's is 'has' joining the pieces

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A political party's revolutionary protest is condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks political but is the reversal signal; 'party's' is a do plus 's for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomed means destined for ruin or death, as a condemned person is.

clue.text: Show one's feelings when reviewing electronic book

indicators.note: re-viewing is looking back over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-book
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A reader becomes emotional while writing a review of an e-book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' turns E TOME round.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display emotion openly, often theatrically, which is showing one's feelings.

clue.text: Rocker to prepare to shoot heroin

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise its hammer ready for firing
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A rock musician gets ready to inject heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' looks like a rock star but means a rocking horse, as in the nursery rhyme 'Ride a cock-horse to Banbury Cross'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock-horse is a child's hobby horse or rocking horse, a toy that rocks back and forth.

clue.text: Courage, passion to overcome resistance

indicators.note: to overcome is to sit on top of and envelop, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: heat means passion or intense feeling
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Bravery and passion are needed to overcome opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heart is to find bravery, so heart is a synonym of courage.

clue.text: Arian poem about Baltic region

indicators.note: about means in a confused state, so the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A heretical Arian poem is written about lands on the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomerania is a historical area on the southern Baltic coast, now split between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: Under canvas, daughter dropped off as day broke

indicators.note: the letter is dropped off the front

parts.note: when day broke it dawned

explanation.surface: A camper in a tent dozed off as day broke, the daughter too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped off' looks like falling asleep but removes D from DAWNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Awned here means sheltered by an awning, a canvas cover, so it describes being beneath canvas.

clue.text: Embarrassed friends every now and again

indicators.note: every now and again means taking letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A person is occasionally embarrassed by their friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, and a blushing face is red with shame.

clue.text: Last bedroom to be renovated? It's No. 28!

indicators.note: a room to be renovated will be rebuilt, so its letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: The final bedroom left for renovation is room number 28.
explanation.walkthrough: No. 28 is the answer at 28 Across, RED; the definition says the answer is red, as the blood flowing through the body is.
explanation.definitionFit: The stream of blood in the circulatory system is bright red in colour, linking it to the 28 Across answer.
